note_to_founders: Most of this I could see in an ordinary week, and the counter-examples are better than I expected: the draft knows what over-counting looks like. Three things before your pass. First, decide what one record is. The draft keeps sliding from a moment to a week, a term, a year, and I cannot carry a term in my head with thirty children; where the child keeps a dated artefact (a plan, a log, a training record) one record of that artefact is fine, but where it is my memory of seven days it is not, so let me write the day and let your system show the pattern. Second, the capture modes were chosen for the evidence and not for the room: a dated note is what I will actually write; keep clips for the debate, the outside presentation and movement, and stop asking for audio in circle time. Third, a few lines are not classroom evidence at all: a private disclosure to a trusted adult, a habit kept at home, a peer supported in confidence. I have skipped them, not because they are untrue but because I will not see them and should not file them. Beyond that: adult_sees mostly repeats the statement; tell me when to stand by the bins, which group to sit with, what to look for on the sheet. Use your own difficulty words, keep Grade 3 under the no-screen rule, and remember that in Pune a third of my timetable is Marathi and Hindi, which this draft does not know exists.
